author: .just_kk
content:
I made a small write up about how we can reduce duplicates during XMSS attestations broadcast.

TLDR largest gain is reducing mesh degree from 8 to 4 (reduces duplicates from 4.3 -> 2.5 per first copy )

Then each peer decides on push or announce by hashing message and peer ids. Another end waits 200ms before requesting the attestation if it still needs it (as on the picture). This further reduces duplicates 2.5 -> 0.9 per first copy. Latency is also improving.

Happy for any feedback. I can also bring this up on tomorrows p2p breakout

https://notes.ethereum.org/@kamilsa/BkFqIVO0ze

author: potuz
content: how does this behave on split scenarios?

author: potuz
content: would it make it much more likely that your mesh quickly becomes from validators on your current branch?

author: .just_kk
content:
what is the split scenario you mean here?

each message has same 50% chance of being either announced or pushed. So peer scoring should not suffer

author: potuz
content: I mean there's a very long fork. If we manage to see blocks and sync them and see attestations and process them the chain heals faster, if we completely split then the chain also heels by actually finalizing both branches eventually. What happens in real life is that some weak nodes in each branch start disconnecting from nodes in the other branch and nodes tend to be connected with other nodes whose head agrees with them. This eventually reinforces the split. If we have smaller meshes my intuition would be that in this situation each node would be more likely to have all of its mesh on the same branch.

author: potuz
content: Continuing on today's aggregation discussion, we should try to bench with the situation in mind that there will be many more than 16 or whatever aggregates for the current slot we have, in particular, every missed slot will double the aggregates that the next proposer needs to include in his block. This already happens today. If this recursion goes linearly, we need to start doing it early. If we allow the aggregators to start doing it then all aggregates for the current slot will have that as an intersection, for BLS this would be wasted computation, not sure how leanVM works with regards to this

author: cskiraly
content:
Those intuitively all check out:
- latency for beefy nodes: less upload capacity in the system, so slower diffusion with lower D
- latency for home nodes: less congestion on their links, net effect could be lower latenct
- lower security: yep, there's a reason we do multi-path diffusion
Of course net effects depend very much on the simulated scenario and how much you managed to capture reality there

author: cskiraly
content:
Yes, in reality less data is sent. In my simulations I've used a compression factor of 1.4:1 (if I remember right). In reality current payloads are above 2:1 (more compressible).
Note that EC parity is not compressible, that's why SEACAST does compress first, segment after, so chunks are balanced at the end
